notes: All five C++ submissions are RTE, so there is no accepted reference. DMOJ serves no statement; tests.toml and gen.py come from the official statement on Luogu P9483 and LOJ 3984, whose four sample files are the inline cases. orig.cpp is a corpus-written reference following the NOI 2023 write-ups' method (linhanpi's notes on GitHub, code/markdown/题解/CCF题解/noi2023.md): a DP over the multiset of per-book move counts layer by layer, where a layer splits the k piles with the least counts and k never falls, so each multiset keeps the (wear, last k) pairs no other pair beats in both, pruned by a lower bound against a greedy schedule. It matches the four official samples, an exponential brute over every merge order on 700 random files (n <= 8, up to 3 cases each), and the previous pruned search on 300 generated files (n <= 100). --max runs in 0.63 s, and the slowest file found (ten copies of the slowest of 400 random n = 100 cases) in 0.80 s, inside the official 1.5 s.
